new_jobs.title: Senior Project Manager - Energy
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM
is seeking a Senior
Project Manager
to support our multi-disciplinary design team addressing the most challenging engineering tasks in power generation. AECOM's broad technical capabilities, global footprint and experience in executing large scale projects uniquely position us to lead in renewable, traditional steam, thermal power generation and advanced nuclear technologies.

This includes being a part of the first-of-a-kind program with AECOM partners advancing the innovative stellarator technology to the world.

https://aecom.com/press-releases/aecom-establishes-partnership-with-type-one-energy-to-provide-design-engineering-services-for-its-innovative-stellarator-fusion-power-plant-infinity-two/

For this role, AECOM offers the freedom and flexibility to work remotely and/or be located at a variety of Energy offices located in multiple locations across the United States.

We seek a project professional able to manage the project lifecycle from the project basis of design stage through the issuance of deliverables, ensuring seamless coordination between internal and external stakeholders.

This position requires a strong understanding of engineering design, interconnection, utility markets, and construction processes. The ideal candidate will possess excellent communication and interpersonal skills, as well as the ability to lead matrixed design teams and manage client-approved engineering consultants.

The successful candidate will:

Responsible for the management of assigned projects; Function as the project manager / program manager
Take ownership of internal project financials, staffing, legal coordination, and risk management.
Facilitate planning and kickoff meetings to ensure alignment among all project stakeholders.
Support projects through complete life cycle including the feasibility phase, preliminary and detailed design, issue-for-bid, construction, start-up, and commissioning
Facilitate the design process, including conducting "page-turn design reviews" and equipment fabrication reviews at key project milestones (30%, 60%, and 100% design completion).
Work closely with the technical delivery team (incl subcontractors) to confirm deliverables and services are being provided to exceed client’s satisfaction. This includes coordination with team members across the world
Deliver projects in accordance with the AECOM Quality Management System (QMS) process
Proposal support / capture leadership to support business development activities
Identify project opportunities early and facilitate go/no-go decisions, determine project fees, write proposals, prepare and lead client presentations, and negotiation of contracts
Client development through existing contracts/relationships including managing key accounts and developing new accounts
Occasional travel to client or project sites

Level specific responsibilities:

Responsible for the overall management administration to project and assists in establishing project specific objectives and policies.
Provides management and guidance to subordinate managers, enforces company and project policies, and a primary liaison between AECOM and client interface.
Oversees and ensures all facets of the project are delivered in accordance with design, budget and schedule through subordinate managers and supervisors.
Responsible for administering the project from budgeting/schedule stage through procurement and contract closeout. Position has significant profit/loss responsibility for assigned project.

AECOM’s Energy practice provides a wide range of services from consulting and engineering design to energy engineering, energy procurement and construction (EPC) for power, energy efficiency, and renewable energy clients. Our understanding of the big picture – and the interconnection between generation, distribution, storage, and the demand side of the meter – allows us to deliver holistic strategies that improve and modernize next generation energy infrastructure. We connect knowledge and experience across our global framework to bring together a unique combination of engineers, planners, scientists, and project managers who advance cleaner, secure, and more sustainable energy solutions.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements:

BA/BS in Electrical, Mechanical Engineering or related degree and 6 years of relevant project management experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
Project Management experience directly related to power generation projects
Demonstrated experience delivering complex engineering projects and/or programs

Preferred Qualifications:

Project Management Professional (PMP)
Professional Engineering Licensure (PE)
Nuclear project experience
+15 Years of relevant experience, power generation or heavy industrial
Experience in managing projects worked in collaborative model environments (e.g. Navisworks, BIM/ACC)
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills to effectively manage diverse teams and stakeholders.
Proven ability to manage large-scale, complex projects in a fast-paced environment.
Demonstrated success working in a remote team environment

Additional Information

Relocation assistance may be available for this position

Sponsorship for US employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $140000 to $180000.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

new_jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager, Foundational Services
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Elevate your career by driving strategic portfolio initiatives that optimize vendor spend, strengthen governance, and improve operational efficiency across Foundational Services.

As a Principal Technical Program Manager
within Foundational Services
, you will lead complex, cross-functional initiatives focused on vendor strategy, spend optimization, contract governance, and portfolio management. You will partner with Product Line Leaders, Finance, Vendor Management, Sourcing, Legal, and Technology stakeholders to drive commercial outcomes while balancing cost, risk, service quality, and strategic objectives. Your advanced analytical reasoning, financial acumen, and ability to influence across organizations will enable you to translate business, technical, financial, and operational priorities into actionable programs that deliver measurable results. In this role, you will help shape governance practices, improve transparency into vendor performance and spending, and establish scalable operating mechanisms that support long-term portfolio management objectives.

This position is subject to Section 19 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act. As such, an employment offer for this position is contingent on JPMorganChase's review of criminal conviction history, including pretrial diversions or program entries.

Job Responsibilities

Develop and implement strategic portfolio management plans aligned with organizational goals, overseeing complex initiatives focused on vendor strategy, spend optimization, contract governance, and commercial performance.
Use enterprise-authorized AI capabilities within the work environment to accelerate portfolio planning, spend analysis, dependency identification, risk synthesis, and executive-ready reporting while validating outputs and handling data according to sensitivity requirements.
Own the Foundational Services vendor spend efficiency agenda, identifying, prioritizing, and tracking cost optimization opportunities across a broad portfolio of products and services.
Lead proactive contract renewal planning, partnering with Vendor Management, Sourcing, Finance, and Legal to coordinate commercial reviews, negotiation strategies, risk assessments, and execution plans.
Establish and maintain vendor strategies across product domains, including vendor rationalization, consolidation opportunities, demand management initiatives, and service-level optimization.
Foster strong relationships with stakeholders and cross-functional teams, providing leadership, governance, and decision-making frameworks that drive beneficial outcomes.
Drive commercial optimization initiatives through benchmarking, pricing model analysis, consumption management, license optimization, rate-card reviews, and identification of duplicative services.
Establish governance forums and operating cadences for spend management, contract oversight, vendor performance reviews, and executive reporting.
Collaborate with Finance to establish spend baselines, validate savings and cost avoidance opportunities, forecast financial impacts, and track benefits realization.
Champion continuous improvement by identifying process optimization opportunities, enhancing portfolio analytics and reporting capabilities, and adopting best practices that improve transparency and decision-making.
Promote reuse-first, AI-assisted practices for portfolio governance and continuous improvement routines while ensuring appropriate human review and compliance with delivery standards.

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills

7+ years of experience or equivalent expertise in technical program management, portfolio management, technology finance, vendor management, sourcing, commercial management, or related disciplines within large organizations (NAMR/APAC-India/LATAM/Hong Kong) Formal training or certification in program management, portfolio management, finance, sourcing, vendor management, or related disciplines with advanced applied experience (EMEA/LATAM-Brazil), Singapore follows local country guidance
Demonstrated experience using enterprise-authorized AI capabilities within the work environment to support portfolio management, financial analysis, governance, and reporting workflows with strong validation habits and awareness of data sensitivity.
Ability to review and validate AI-assisted plans, risks, recommendations, financial analyses, and reporting outputs before use, escalating when appropriate and following data handling requirements.
Advanced analytical reasoning skills with the ability to synthesize spend, contract, operational, and financial data into actionable recommendations and strategic decisions.
Strong understanding of vendor commercial constructs, including licensing models, consumption-based pricing, renewal terms, volume tiers, benchmarking methodologies, notice periods, and contractual obligations.
Proven ability to lead through change, manage complex dependencies, and drive execution across multiple stakeholders in dynamic environments.
Experience delivering measurable cost optimization, savings, cost avoidance, or operational efficiency initiatives supported by disciplined governance and benefits realization practices.
Advanced expertise in stakeholder management, establishing productive partnerships and influencing outcomes across Product, Engineering, Operations, Finance, Sourcing, Vendor Management, and Legal organizations.
Strong executive communication skills, including governance leadership, concise written communications, presentation development, and issue escalation management.
Advanced proficiency with Excel and experience leveraging analytical and business intelligence tools such as Power BI, Tableau, SQL, Power Query, Alteryx, Python, or comparable technologies.

Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills

Experience supporting Foundational Services, infrastructure platforms, enterprise tooling, end-user services, managed services, security services, or similar technology domains.
Experience operating in a regulated environment with exposure to third-party risk management, resiliency requirements, vendor performance management, and governance controls.
Demonstrated success building scalable operating mechanisms such as renewal pipelines, vendor scorecards, quarterly business reviews, category strategies, and portfolio governance frameworks.
Strong understanding of infrastructure, technology operations, and enterprise service delivery cost drivers, including capacity, utilization, consumption patterns, entitlements, and service levels.
Experience developing executive-level portfolio dashboards, financial reporting, and strategic planning materials for senior leadership.

About Us

JPMorganChase, one of the oldest financial institutions, offers innovative financial solutions to millions of consumers, small businesses and many of the world's most prominent corporate, institutional and government clients under the J.P. Morgan and Chase brands. Our history spans over 200 years and today we are a leader in investment banking, consumer and small business banking, commercial banking, financial transaction processing and asset management.

We offer a competitive total rewards package including base salary determined based on the role, experience, skill set and location. Those in eligible roles may receive commission-based pay and/or discretionary incentive compensation, paid in the form of cash and/or forfeitable equity, awarded in recognition of individual achievements and contributions. We also offer a range of benefits and programs to meet employee needs, based on eligibility. These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage, on-site health and wellness centers, a retirement savings plan, backup childcare, tuition reimbursement, mental health support, financial coaching and more. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided during the hiring process.

We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. Visit our FAQs for more information about requesting an accommodation.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including Disability/Veterans

About The Team

Our Global Technology Infrastructure group is a team of innovators who love technology as much as you do. Together, you'll use a disciplined, innovative and a business focused approach to develop a wide variety of high-quality products and solutions. You'll work in a stable, resilient and secure operating environment where you—and the products you deliver—will thrive.

new_jobs.title: Engineering Program Manager, Devices
new_jobs.description:
About Atomic Machines:

Atomic Machines is ushering in a new era of micromanufacturing with its Matter Compiler™ technology platform. This platform enables new classes of micromachines to be designed and built by providing manufacturing processes and a materials library that are inaccessible to semiconductor manufacturing methods. It unlocks MEMS manufacturing not only for device classes that could never be produced by semiconductor methods, but also for entirely new categories. Furthermore, this digital platform is fully programmable in the way 3D printing is digital, but whereas 3D printing produces parts of a single material using a single process, the Matter Compiler™ technology platform is a multi-process, multi-material system: bits and raw materials go in, and complete, functional micromachines come out. The Atomic Machines team has also created an exciting first device, made possible only through the Matter Compiler™ technology platform, addressing a critical need in the rapidly evolving AI data center world, and we are commercializing it now.

Our offices are in Emeryville and Santa Clara, California.

About The Role:

We are seeking a highly technical Engineering Program Manager to own the program for that first device's successor, end to end: from requirements still maturing with lead customers, through qualification, certification, and manufacturing scale-up on the Matter Compiler, to commercial launch. That successor is a new class of micromachine, made possible only by the Matter Compiler, and you will be the leader that delivers it.

At Atomic Machines, Program Management is a leverage function, and its core skill is clarity. The Device program's technical leadership is already in place: device design, process, test, and reliability are each led by deep domain owners who move fast and expect the same. You lead that team as one program, and you drive the outcome, integrated plan, customer commitments, tradeoffs, operating cadence, and decisions that keep every discipline moving as one. Technical direction belongs to the domain owners; turning their work into the outcomes of certified, scaling, revenue-generating products belongs to you. This role is for someone who was an individual contributor in complex technical domains and moved into program leadership on purpose: to influence product direction, align engineering and manufacturing, and own outcomes end to end.

What You'll Do:

Develop and drive the program roadmap end to end: set goals, define milestones and evidence gates, and build the accountability structure that connects daily engineering work to business outcomes and customer commitments.
Direct cross-functional execution across device physics, fabrication processes, automation, and system integration: set the deliverables, sequencing, and resource calls for engineering, operations, and leadership.
Build and run the integrated plan connecting customer commitments, design maturity, process capability, and manufacturing readiness. Run the operating cadence that keeps it honest.
Turn maturing customer requirements into committed, testable targets, and hold the program to them.
Build the program structures that keep device and process development in lockstep with the Matter Compiler platform. Move development from R&D into production and define what each handoff must prove.
Structure the program around evidence and short learning loops: design the build-test-learn iteration cycles, give every open unknown an experiment with a pass/fail criterion, and let the schedule follow from results.
Own the qualification and certification path (e.g., UL/IEC) as a program commitment shaped into the design from day one.
Deliver the outcome: the device demonstrated, evaluated by lead customers, and qualified through production ramp.
Institutionalize what you learn: build the systems, rhythms, and decision structures the whole organization runs on, so the next program moves faster than this one.

What You'll Need:

8+ years spanning hands-on engineering and technical program leadership on complex multidisciplinary hardware: you have personally taken things from thought to build and owned programs that others depended on.
A track record of taking integrated hardware systems from concept through manufacturing release and commercial delivery, with the judgment to know when a decision needs more rigor and when to move fast.
Deep technical fluency in at least one core engineering domain and productive command across the rest: you hold your own with engineers designing in coupled physical domains — electromagnetics, structural mechanics, thermal behavior, fluidics, and materials.
You drive senior technical leads to deliver at a high level: clarity, structure, and pace, while technical direction stays with the domain owner.
Relentlessness in driving through ambiguity: turning unresolved requirements into scope, evidence gates, and a plan the team runs.
Conviction in iterative hardware development and short learning loops — build early, test early, learn fast, continually finding the shortest learning loop.
True Ownership of your program and domain, with bottom-line-up-front communication, trusted by engineers and leadership alike. The strongest people you've worked with would choose to work with you again.
BS or higher in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Materials Science.

Nice to Have:

Reliability engineering for microscale or precision devices: accelerated life testing, environmental stress testing, and long-term performance characterization.
Experience driving a product through UL, IEC, or equivalent certification.
Experience standing up programs from ground zero, then driving reliability growth to manufacturing scale.

You will investigate carrier feedback at scale, synthesizing signals and routing prioritized insights to the appropriate product and engineering teams to drive systemic improvements.

You will be the connective tissue between operations, product, engineering, and senior leadership, bridging technical depth with executive-level storytelling. You will own business goal tracking for the organization, building mechanisms that ensure accountability across multiple teams and organizations for issue resolution and action item closure. You should be able to apply a breadth of tools, data sources, and analytical techniques to answer a wide range of high-impact business questions and proactively present new insights in a concise and effective manner.

The ideal candidate thrives in ambiguity, can context-switch between a deep technical investigation and an executive-ready narrative within the same day, and has a bias for action when it comes to closing gaps. You will work directly with partners across product management, engineering, data science, and operations to ensure our reporting infrastructure is robust, our metrics are trustworthy, and our leadership has the information they need to make both high-quality and high-velocity decisions.

Key job responsibilities

Own the end-to-end business reporting within the TTS organization for Delivery Accuracy within Middle Mile, delivering high-fidelity operational insights to Director and VP-level audiences on a daily, weekly, monthly, and quarterly cadence
Drive cross-org VP and SVP-level goals related to improving Middle Mile Delivery Accuracy.
Operate within a culture of escalate and debate
Conduct rigorous operational deep dives to identify root causes and failure modes within business logic, data pipelines, SOPs, and technology systems, translating findings into actionable recommendations and driving resolution through cross-functional coordination
Partner with business stakeholders, product teams, and engineering to align on reporting priorities and ensure shared visibility into program health and goal attainment
Support in working with other product and program managers globally to identify reporting gaps, systemic issues, and opportunities for process and tooling improvement
Dive deep into data to uncover reporting discrepancies, metric anomalies, and operational trends that unlock new opportunities for improvement
Investigate and synthesize carrier feedback at scale, distilling actionable themes and routing prioritized insights to the appropriate product and engineering teams with clear context and recommended next steps
Own business goal tracking for the organization, building and maintaining mechanisms that ensure transparency into progress, blockers, and risk across multiple teams and senior leadership
Create, maintain, and disseminate program information to stakeholders and leadership across the organization via business reviews, flash reports, and operational readouts, identifying potential bottlenecks, dependencies, or project risks
Drive cross-organizational accountability for issue tracking, escalation management, and action item closure; establishing mechanisms that ensure nothing falls through the cracks
Partner across product and engineering teams to apply new technologies, automation, and tooling to improve reporting infrastructure and operational efficiency

A day in the life

On any given day, you might start by investigating an anomaly that resulted in a customer promise miss, tracing it through reporting logic and tech systems to identify the root cause. By mid-morning, you're synthesizing carrier feedback into a concise brief for the Operations and Product team, then pivoting to prepare a business review narrative for senior leadership (Director/VP). Afternoons could involve driving accountability in a cross-functional stand-up with operations, program management, and product managers, tracking action items to closure, or building the weekly operational readout that keeps our organization aligned. Your internal stakeholders span Product, Engineering, Program Management, and Operations Supply Chain leadership. Your customers are the senior leaders who depend on accurate, timely insights to make high-quality decisions, and the product, program, and operations teams who rely on your investigations to prioritize the right problems.

About The Team

The Technology Transportation Services (TTS) organization builds software systems that work across our vendors, warehouses and carriers to optimize both time and cost of getting the packages delivered. Our services already handle thousands of requests per second, make business decisions impacting billions of dollars a year, integrate with a network of small and large carriers, owner operators and drivers worldwide, manage business rules for millions of unique products, and improve ordering and delivery experience for millions of online shoppers. That said, this remains a fast growing business and our technical journey has only started. With rapid expansion into new geographies, innovations in supply chain, unique delivery models for products ranging from Amazon Fresh groceries, ultra-fast Prime Now deliveries of big-screen TV’s, increasingly complex transportation network, and growing number of shipments worldwide, we see a massive opportunity to fundamentally change the way people get the stuff they need, and make a big impact by cutting billions of dollars of transportation costs from the ecosystem. Our mission is to build the most efficient and optimal transportation solution on the planet, using our science and technology muscle as our biggest advantage.

Who we are
Arena Physica is on a mission to accelerate hardware innovation that powers human progress. Our name is inspired by Theodore Roosevelt's 'Citizenship in a Republic' speech. To us, entering the Arena means committing fully and accepting the risk of failure in pursuit of an audacious, worthy cause. We believe the future belongs to those brave enough to build it.

Our team of 50 combines AI engineering and applied physics expertise with deep experience in enterprise deployments. We're headquartered in NYC with presences in San Francisco and Los Angeles, backed by ~$90M from Initialized, Founders Fund, Goldcrest Capital, Fifth Down Capital, and Shield Capital.

If you're ready to do the most important work of your career, join us in the Arena.

What we do
At Arena Physica, we're building electromagnetic superintelligence. Our AI platform Atlas operationalizes physics-grounded intelligence to verify, debug, and optimize hardware across its lifecycle. Atlas is already trusted globally by the world's most advanced hardware companies, including AMD, Anduril, and Bausch & Lomb, for applications across R&D, integration testing, production assembly, and field repair.

About the role
As a Deployment Strategist, you will own the success of an Atlas deployment from end to end—from use case identification and workflow mapping to new feature development that accelerate hardware innovation.

Working on fast timelines, you'll collaborate closely with customers, users, and Arena Physica's engineering, and GTM teams to successfully deploy Atlas, while measuring and demonstrating real-world value. Your responsibilities include building a deep understanding of your users, their organizations, and their workflows, then identifying how new or existing Atlas features will transform their processes. You'll work directly with customers to remove technical and organizational blockers, making you a key player in their success.

In close collaboration with our engineering team, you'll work with Arena Physica's Head of Forward Deployed Engineering and Head of Product to identify and develop new features that deliver maximum value to users in real-world scenarios. This is a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience driving innovation across some of the world's most vital industries — ideal for those aspiring to become founders or product leaders.

How you will contribute
Deployment ownership - own deployment execution for one or more customer accounts from technical strategy to stakeholder management, and develop deep understanding of our users. Ensure deployment success through consistent on-site presence and building strong relationships across the organization.
Drive user adoption - drive usage of Atlas with our customers, and provide structured, technical product feedback to our Core Product and Platform engineering teams to shape our product roadmap.
Foster and grow relationships with users and senior technical/business leadership - lead technical conversations with senior customer leadership and technical users as our domain expert at the intersection of AI and Electrical Engineering.
Travel domestically and internationally (up to 50% of your time)
Work in person at Arena Physica's NYC HQ when not traveling

You have
4+ years of professional experience, ideally as an engineer or TPM working in industry – at a leading company in Aerospace, Automotive or Semiconductors
Full-stack technical literacy - you are well versed across a wide range of technical topics with deep expertise in select areas, and you are eager and able to pick up new depths easily
Product-fluency - you have worked closely with product teams, understand the user journey, and can balance technical product development with practical user needs.
A strong ability to understand and articulate how AI-native products create commercial value
Strong written and verbal communication & storytelling – you can communicate your ideas clearly and concisely in a medium of your choosing to a wide variety of stakeholders

Benefits & Perks Include:
100% of the monthly premium for Aetna medical insurance, plus vision and dental coverage
401(k) Retirement Plan
Unlimited PTO
Lunch every day from local restaurants via Sharebite
Relocation support provided

Director

Solid knowledge of core functions of an insurance company and general insurance (knowledge of Underwriting process highly preferred).
Solid technical knowledge of financial, economical and statistical practices, procedures and principles, which may include a specialty area of the business.

Primary job duties and responsibilities may include, but are not limited to the following:

Establish a process for strategic deconfliction in collaboration with internal and external aviation stakeholders for a new FAA Traffic Flow Management Evolution Program for a potential “24/7” operation
Work 40 hours a week but potentially work late night shifts and weekends at times to cover overnight and weekend data modeling needs
Collect historical data, observe network of applicable systems in action, and interview stakeholders to understand operational bottlenecks and business process inefficiencies
Using programming languages, along with specialized software, to potentially build quantitative models to simulate various scenarios
Help determine the most efficient and ideal best course of action (e.g., build data models that translate to lower fuel burden, less aircraft downtime, shorter block times, and faster flights) given a strict set of real-world constraints
Document the FAA process, roles, and responsibilities to enable execution of strategic deconfliction process plan for day of operations in the National Airspace System (NAS) Work with FAA and industry vendor(s) who will architect and build the analytical data model and provide feedback as necessary
Collaborate with FAA stakeholders and external industry partners (as needed) to obtain necessary data to operate logistically optimized model
Enter data into analytical models (long range and same day planning) to develop strategic deconfliction plans
As needed, support the training of FAA staff on process execution related to newly designed traffic flow management program
Document all lessons learned and FAA process improvement opportunities for evolution of strategic deconfliction processes/capability
Apply knowledge in the domain of operations research to optimize NAS strategic deconfliction plan
Define post event analysis criteria and data expectations
Document recommended process improvement opportunities
Provide expertise in the design, development, implementation, and analysis of technical FAA products and systems

The Successful Candidate Will Have

Have deep expertise in data collection and modeling in support of the federal government and preferably in support of FAA mission
Deep analytical thinking, strong programming skills, and the ability to translate highly technical data into actionable, strategic recommendations for non-technical stakeholders
Have some background in air traffic management and airport operations including FAA traffic flow management practices
Possess broad knowledge of operations research procedures, methodologies, and can provide technical expertise in the application of state-of-the-art technology to meet FAA mission and aerospace requirements
Flexible work schedule that may require working at FAA in-person and cover nights, weekends and even some holidays during the year as this is in support of a national and highly visible FAA project
Potentially be on call to cover shifts when anticipated higher days of operations or team members are unavailable/on scheduled vacation
Must have at least 10 years of professional years of experience supporting projects as an Operations Research Analyst but preferably in support of the FAA/NASA or at least the federal government
Must have a Bachelor of Science Degree in engineering (e.g. Engineering, Operations Research, Statistics, Computer Science, Mathematics) or related field

Salary: $120,000 to $130,000 annually. Compensation is based on relevant experience and qualifications.

Tetra Tech is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified candidates will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sex, marital or familial status, status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by law. Tetra Tech is a VEVRAA federal contractor and we request priority referral of veterans.

Job Title: Senior Financial Health Data Analyst

Location: Hybrid - Honolulu, Hawaii ( 2 days onsite per week)

Employment Type: 12+ Months (With potential to become FTE)

Job Summary

We are seeking a Senior Financial Health Data Analyst I
to provide financial management, analysis, and reporting support for government and commercial programs, health plans, and provider contracts of our client. This role focuses on contract compliance, financial stewardship, benefit cost management, reimbursement strategies, data quality, and process improvement
. The successful candidate will analyze financial and operational data, identify trends and cost-reduction opportunities, support provider and program initiatives, and develop meaningful reports for management. The position operates with moderate management direction and oversight.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree and three years of related work experience, or an equivalent combination of education and related work experience.
Demonstrated experience with budgeting, forecasting, and variance analysis
.
Basic knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint.
Intermediate working knowledge of Microsoft Excel
.

Key Responsibilities

Financial & Provider Analysis

Analyze, recommend, and monitor reimbursement and provider strategies.
Prepare reports measuring the effectiveness of reimbursement and contracting terms and their impact on program costs and utilization.
Analyze data to identify trends, patterns, issues, and opportunities for cost reduction.
Monitor market trends and identify emerging business opportunities and risks.
Monitor private and government websites for reimbursement and policy changes and recommend appropriate implementation.

Reporting & Business Analysis

Analyze standard plan, provider, financial, and operational reports in response to customer and business requirements.
Develop functional summary reports and presentations for management.
Facilitate the definition of data and information requirements.
Establish efficient methods for assembling and maintaining data.
Maintain appropriate documentation for reference and audit purposes.

Proactively identify potential data or process issues.
Work collaboratively with internal and external teams to develop and implement solutions.

Identify opportunities to improve productivity, efficiency, and overall business value.
Help transform existing processes and policies to make them more effective and efficient.

Compliance & Contract Management

.
Review provider contracts and verify that claims system configurations accurately reflect fully executed agreements.
Support contract compliance and financial stewardship initiatives.

Team Leadership & Collaboration

Participate in and promote team activities.
Provide leadership, consultation, and subject-matter expertise on projects.
Share accountability and knowledge across the team.
Communicate effectively with stakeholders and provide constructive feedback.
Support initiatives that improve workflow integrity and operational effectiveness.

new_jobs.title: Project Manager II
new_jobs.description:
Job ID: req4669

Employee Type: exempt full-time

Division: Vaccine, Immunity and Cancer Directorate

Facility: Frederick: ATRF

Location: 8560 Progress Dr, Frederick, MD 21701 USA

The Frederick National Laboratory is operated by Leidos Biomedical Research, Inc. The lab addresses some of the most urgent and intractable problems in the biomedical sciences in cancer and AIDS, drug development and first-in-human clinical trials, applications of nanotechnology in medicine, and rapid response to emerging threats of infectious diseases.

Accountability, Compassion, Collaboration, Dedication, Integrity and Versatility; it's the FNL way.

Program Description

The Vaccine, Immunity and Cancer Directorate (VICD) has a primary mission to provide scientific leadership and laboratory infrastructure to study immune responses to Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines and other cancer preventive strategies in the context of preclinical and clinical studies. As of recent and part of a large effort, the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) and the Frederick National Laboratory (FNL) and other stakeholders are developing vaccines with durable protection for seasonal influenza virus. VICD is leading the development of immunoassays with the highest reproducibility, sensitivity, and specificity for evaluation of immune responses against the virus and vaccine.

VICD is recruiting for a Cross Functional Project Manager II to provide cross functional project management and programmatic operations. The ideal candidate will have prior experience working in a laboratory under the Good Clinical Laboratory Practices or GxP and is familiar with laboratory operations. The Cross Functional Project Manager II will report to the Director, Program and Operations, working with program directors, scientific managers and across matrix to meet the program and project goals, and assist and drive program activities to meet the deadlines for deliverables.

Key Roles/Responsibilities

Assist in the management of research subcontracts supporting the program
Manage administrative Program activities by performing a variety of high-level administrative and programmatic functions that include planning and implementation of overall Program strategies
Communicate effectively to compose both business and scientific documents and ensure efficient Program operations
Assist with overall coordination of Program/Project level functions
Ensure Program compliance with all policies and procedures related to project management, contract relations, purchasing, and fiscal planning
Provide meeting management support to Programs, including drafting agendas, meeting notes/minutes and recording, monitoring and follow-up action items with internal and external stakeholders as needed
Assist in the preparation of program reports, including monthly quarterly reports, semi-annual and annual reports
Assists with progress reporting, deliverables, and proposals, statement of work, and 508 compliance, other formal documents, formatting, editing, and submissions to appropriate systems and to stakeholders
Assist with personnel actions such as requisition postings, onboarding and off-boarding activities such as office setup, computer and equipment setup, folder access, etc.
Assists in the development of oral presentations and meetings with internal and external stakeholders
Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders for intellectual property requirements, CRADAs, MTAs, collaboration agreements, subcontracts
Work with managers to ensure laboratory and programs are operating in an efficient manner, providing administrative/operation support
Working directly with the laboratory to perform equipment request processing, equipment management, coordinating vendors to certification completion
Data entry for biological material inventory on an annual basis with accuracy Liaise with internal groups and other LBR groups (HR, Finance, Purchasing, Equipment, etc.) as required
Perform other related duties as assigned

Basic Qualifications

To be considered for this position, you must minimally meet the knowledge, skills, and abilities listed below:

Possession of Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college/university according to the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) or four (4) years relevant experience in lieu of degree. Foreign degrees must be evaluated for U.S. equivalency
In addition to the education requirement, a minimum of two (2) years of related experience managing research, experimental planning, proposal writing and project management
Working knowledge and facility with Microsoft Office Suite
Ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance

Preferred Qualifications

Candidates with these desired skills will be given preferential consideration:

Regulatory knowledge pertinent to standards GCLP, CLIA or FDA guidelines for clinical assays
Familiarity with immunoassays, testing, equipment maintenance, LIMS
Knowledge of CostPoint, Cognos, Corcentric, ERP
Knowledge of finance and budgeting
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification

EXPECTED COMPETENCIES

In-depth understanding of immunology, immune assays, diagnostics, vaccines and clinical research
Excellent communications skills (written and oral)
Ability to work effectively in a matrix and team-oriented environment
Ability to identify and solve complex problems
Strong organizationand multitasking skills

JOB HAZARDS

This position is subject to working with or has the potential for exposure to infectious material, requiring medical clearance and immunizations.

Commitment to Non-Discrimination

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, ethnicity, color, age, national origin, citizenship, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, pregnancy, family structure, marital status, ancestry, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran or military status, or any other basis prohibited by law. Leidos will also consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories consistent with relevant laws.

Pay And Benefits

Pay and benefits are fundamental to any career decision. That's why we craft compensation packages that reflect the importance of the work we do for our customers. Employment benefits include competitive compensation, Health and Wellness programs, Income Protection, Paid Leave and Retirement. More details are available here

79,300.00 - 116,630.00 USD

The posted pay range for this job is a general guideline and not a guarantee of compensation or salary. Additional factors considered in extending an offer include, but are not limited to, responsibilities of the job, education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities as well as internal equity, and alignment with market data.

The salary range posted is a full-time equivalent salary and will vary depending on scheduled hours for part time positions

Job Summary

Leidos is seeking a Deputy Program Manager
to support a high-impact, multi-agency program serving the United States Space Force (USSF)/Space Systems Command (SSC), the United States Air Force (USAF), and other key mission stakeholders. This position will support program execution across financial performance, workforce management, customer engagement, and contractual compliance, ensuring successful mission outcomes.

Responsibilities include tracking program status against customer and corporate requirements, supporting Earned Value Management reporting, aligning resources to program needs, preparing briefings and program documentation, responding to customer and company data calls, and helping resolve administrative and business issues. Oversee all program administrative and business operations, including Subcontracts, Earned Value Management, Finance, and Security.
Serve as a key Point of Contact for the Contracting Officer (CO), Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR), Government Program Manager, and company senior leadership, including executive-level stakeholders.
Lead program operations in the absence of the Program Manager (PM) or when the PM is engaged in other critical program priorities.
Maintain full comprehensive awareness of program activities and serve as a secondary Point of Contact between program staff and Government stakeholders.
Manage operational execution and financial performance for contract deliverables, cost, and schedule to ensure achievement of all key performance indicators and annual operating plan commitments.
Ensure compliance with contractual requirements, the Statement of Work, and Leidos policies and procedures.
Serve as Control Account Manager (CAM) for the Program Management Office account.
Lead and support customer and internal meetings, including agenda development, coordination, and follow-up.
Prepare program reporting materials, including inputs for IPR, PSR, IPMDAR, and other formal reviews for Senior Leadership and Government PMOstakeholders.
Partner with functional support teams to ensure customer and company requirements are fully met.
Collaborate with highly technical teams to track program status and provide operational and management support as needed.
Coordinate the development of Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs) and support business development activities.
Review and approve Earned Value, Estimate to Complete, and other financial reports, as appropriate.
Communicate program issues, risks, and solutions to the Government Program Manager in a timely and transparent manner,as required.
Contribute to, review, and ensure the timely delivery of Program Management CDRL deliverables.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree and at least 12 years of relevant experience. Additional experience may be substituted for a degree.
At least ten (10) years of experience as a Program or Project Manager, leading programs and contracts of significant scope, type, complexity, and impact.
At least one (1)year of experience managing and controlling program funds and resources using advanced reporting methods, including Earned Value Management (EVM).
Demonstrated experience in requirements analysis, resource allocation, project costing, deliverable tracking, and schedule and financial performance monitoring.
Proven leadership experience managing both direct reports and cross-functional teams.
Experience managing multiple subcontractors and teammates in support of program execution.
Strong ability to apply sound judgment and effective problem-solving skills in complex, fast-paced environments.
Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communications skills.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple high-priority issues and tasks simultaneously in a dynamic environment.
Strong ability to plan, prioritize, and execute work proactively with a demonstrated ability to take initiative and resolve issues quickly and directly as they arise.
Clearance Required: Must have TS/SCI with Polygraph.

Preferred Qualifications

PMP, FAC-P/PM Mid-Level, or Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement Act (DAWIA) Level II certification in Program Management.
Experience applying Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) methodologies in support of program execution.
Demonstrated experience executing Earned Value Management (EVM) on a large, complex program.
At least five (5) years of experience supporting large-scale software development and hardware integration programs.
At least two (2) years of experience working in an Agile program environment.

Description

Leidos has an opportunity for a Technical Project Manager on the DISA Cross Domain Enterprise Services (CDES) effort. This position is a technical position that supports both engineering and cross domain specific technical areas across multiple doctrines and domains for full life cycle engineering, testing, policy, deployment and sustainment of the DISA Cross Domain Enterprise Services (CDES). The selected candidate must be able to work primarily on-site at DISA Headquarters in Fort Meade, MD.

This critical role is responsible for the management and timely execution of CDES engineering projects, CDS Approval rhythms and compliance, documentation and operation support activities and must balance programmatic support with mission and operational-focused priorities. Candidates must demonstrate experience in aspects of project management, customer engagement, lead and develop implementation of complex engineering and network solutions, while leading a team of engineers and A&A team members. This is not a people leader position.

Primary Responsibilities

Lead engineering projects on behalf of the program managing day-to-day engineering management for CDES efforts, including managing schedules, requirements, testing, integration, deployment, documentation, reporting, work allocation, engineering delivery and full life cycle product development.
Work with managers and the program leadership team to ensure program initiatives and vision is being executed and enforced through engineering teams.
Identify program and project risks and employ mitigations, resolve issues throughout the project lifecycle, track and report project milestones, document and execute action plans, and make decisions and recommendations based on business needs.
Work closely with engineers, RMF SMEs, and program leadership to establish and enforce cross-functional processes and procedures and establish standard policies and procedures.
Supervise technical projects / high-priority engineering tasks in conjunction with other responsibilities.
Work as primary liaison for Customer and Mission Partner communication and engagement.
Manage workflow of Cross Domain Approval boards and interactions with outside agencies.
Participate in staffing/recruiting and retention efforts and personnel management, including selection and training, work assignments in conduction with management.
Motivate and lead team members, fostering a diverse and inclusive environment.
Effectively communicate with Leidos leadership, customer leadership. program staff, subcontract partners, and other stakeholders.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree and 8+ years of directly relevant experience, including providing expertise on multiple complex assignments, developing methodology and developing/presenting solutions to problems, and managing personnel. Additional experience may be considered in lieu of degree.
Active Secret security clearance up to TS/SCI.
DoD 8570 IAT-II Certification (Sec +) or higher
Highly proficient in a software engineering discipline (developer, network engineer, cross domain experience)
Understanding of Git or other code and configuration management tools.
Cross Domain Experience to included knowledge of RTB, NCDSMO and NSA requirements.
Excellent written and verbal communication, leadership, organization, and time-management skills
Experience managing program delivering systems/tools/solutions in production, while transitioning to better technology solutions.
Experience working with DISA or DoD customer(s) on projects related to sustainment activities of the Defense Information Systems Network (DISN) infrastructure.

Preferred Qualifications

Familiar with DISA networks and processes.
Cross Domain Approval Process Understanding
Working knowledge of software and network development
Hands on working knowledge of cross domain technologies and tools
Extensive knowledge of Excel, to include but not limited data manipulation, formulas, pivot tables, representing data in graphical formats.

Description

Leidos has an opportunity for a cyber professional to join our team at Fort Meade in Maryland. This is a hybrid position based primarily on-site, with opportunity for 1-2 remote days per week depending on mission needs.

This position will support the implementation and administration of information security policies, procedures, and technologies to ensure the protection of systems, applications, and data on tactical and development networks.

Primary Responsibilities

Support the Assessment and Authorization of DoD systems, software, and networks in accordance with the Risk Management Framework (RMF), utilizing the Enterprise Mission Assurance Support Service (eMASS) system.
Provide professional security services for IA/Cybersecurity in accordance with US Government (USG), Department of Defense (DoD) and National Security Agency (NSA) policies and guidelines.
Provide the necessary support to monitor and ensure compliance with information security policies, procedures and regulatory requirements including assistance with internal auditing, reporting, technical reviews, and identification of security risks.- Assist with drafting, reviewing, editing, and recommending guidance for Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), Tactics, Techniques, & Procedures (TTP), System Security Plans (SSP), Plan Of Action and Milestones (POA&M), and Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA).
Support the implementation and administration of information security policies, procedures, and technologies to ensure the protection of systems, applications, and data on tactical and development networks by working hand and hand with technical SMEs, systems administrators and engineers.

Basic Qualifications

Active DoD Secret clearance.
Bachelor's Degree and 8+ years of experience. Additional years of professional and/or military experience may be substituted in lieu of degree.
Must possess DoD 8140 (formerly 8570) IAT Level II certification (e.g., Security+) prior to start date.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Cross Domain Solutions and Secret and Below Interoperability (SABI) framework, process and implementation
Experience in performing risk assessment, IT audits, security planning, systems accreditation and policy development.
Experience complying with USG, DoD, and DA regulations and preparing for responding to information security audits and questionnaires.
Understanding of related information technology (e.g. firewalls, VPN, virtualization, DLP, etc) and physical security assets.
Knowledge of domain structures, user authentication, data encryption, access audits and end-user security best practices.
Experience with UNIX/LINUX OS and any scripting language.
Experience working with IDS/IPS and processes.

new_jobs.title: ERP Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

Work Location:
Remote - U.S. Based. Candidates within driving distance of our Reston, VA office are preferred for occasional in-person meetings, but proximity to Reston is not required.

Duration:
Full Time

Travel:
Occasional travel for client requests and/or XTIVIA in-office meetings, up to 25%.

How You Will Make a Difference

XTIVIA is looking for an ERP Project Manager to lead client-facing ERP implementation projects from planning through delivery. In this role, you will manage project timelines, budgets, resources, risks, and client expectations while working closely with functional and technical teams to keep multiple projects moving successfully.

You will serve as a key connection between our clients and internal teams, ensuring projects remain on track, issues are addressed proactively, and stakeholders have clear visibility throughout the implementation lifecycle.

Responsibilities

Project Delivery: Lead ERP projects using effective project management practices to achieve project goals on time and within budget while proactively identifying and managing risks.
Client Communication: Communicate project status, client readiness, business and technical issues, risks, decisions, and resolutions to clients, project teams, and management.
Budget & Resource Management: Monitor project budgets and funding expenditures while helping define, acquire, and allocate the staff and resources necessary to accomplish project objectives.
Financial Forecasting: Accurately forecast project labor hours and resource needs to support revenue planning and overall project performance.
Risk & Issue Management: Use project management, financial, and accounting tools to identify and assess project risks and coordinate issue tracking through resolution.
Project Documentation: Develop and maintain clear project documentation, diagrams, status reports, meeting materials, and other communications needed to support successful delivery.
Resource Coordination: Work closely with internal teams to ensure appropriate XTIVIA resources are available to support project needs and drive recommendations through implementation.
Client Relationships: Build and maintain strong client relationships throughout consulting engagements, with a focus on communication, trust, and client satisfaction.
Change Control: Coordinate client change control processes to effectively manage changes to project scope, timelines, resources, and expectations.
Project & Process Improvement: Contribute to project analysis and process improvement activities, identifying opportunities to strengthen project delivery and client outcomes.
Progress Reporting: Monitor and report on project progress while keeping stakeholders informed of milestones, dependencies, risks, and next steps.
Concurrent Project Management: Effectively manage multiple client projects and competing priorities at the same time.

Requirements

What you bring to your new team

A bachelor's degree in a relevant field or equivalent professional experience.
2 to 5 years of experience working with ERP software as a consultant and/or Project Manager.
At least 1 year of experience in a client-facing project management role.
Experience supporting ERP implementation projects and managing activities throughout the project lifecycle.
Strong time management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and priorities.
Strong customer relationship skills and experience working directly with clients.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate comfortably with stakeholders at all levels of an organization.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work collaboratively with functional, technical, and business teams.
Proficiency with G Suite and Microsoft Office, including Microsoft Project and Visio.
Experience using project management and collaboration tools such as Salesforce, Jira, Monday.com, Smartsheet, or similar systems.

new_jobs.title: Payments & Risk Operations Manager
new_jobs.description:
About Cantina

Cantina Labs is a social AI company, developing a suite of advanced real-time models that push the boundaries of expression, personality, and realism. We bring characters to life, transforming how people tell stories, connect, and create. We build and power ecosystems. Cantina, our flagship social AI platform, is just the beginning.

If you're excited about the potential AI has to shape human creativity and social interactions, join us in building the future!

About The Role

Cantina.ai is building a commerce business—subscriptions, credits, and payments—and we're looking for the person who will own customer support for it.

You won't be doing this alone. Executives and teammates across Product, Engineering, and Operations are already invested in getting this right. Your job is to turn that shared focus into a support function that actually works, day to day.

Early on, that means rolling up your sleeves: working tickets yourself, building the first workflows, and getting a system in place fast. As volume grows, you'll shift toward setting direction, managing our vendor partners for billing and payments and overflow customer support capacity, and knowing which cases need Product, Engineering, or leadership rather than your own hands.

We think this is a great fit for someone 3-7 years into their career who's run support or support ops before, enjoys building something new alongside people who care about it, and wants real ownership over how it takes shape.

The role reports into Operations and works closely with the Product and Engineering teams behind subscriptions. It starts as an individual contributor role with high ownership; and as the business scales, you'll help decide whether and how the team grows with it.

What You'll Do

Own day-to-day customer support across eCommerce. Handle billing questions, cancellations, refunds, credit balance and top-up issues, failed or disputed payments, access issues, and general customer inquiries directly, especially early on while volume is low and workflows are still taking shape.
Own payments risk operations. Monitor fraud, refund abuse, disputes and chargeback patterns; investigate anomalous transaction and account behavior; develop policies and operational controls that balance loss prevention with a low-friction customer experience; and partner with Product, Engineering and our payment provider on improvements to authorization, fraud prevention and dispute performance.
Create and maintain the playbook. Build support workflows, macros, escalation paths, and SLAs across subscriptions, credits, and payments, working closely with the executives and teammates across Product, Engineering, and Operations who are also focused on getting this right.
Leverage and manage the payment platform relationship. Own billing operations with our payments platform day to day—disputes, chargebacks, failed payments, refund workflows, credit/balance adjustments, and reconciliation questions—coordinating with Finance as needed.
Leverage and manage the outsourced operations relationship. Serve as the primary point of contact with our outsourced operations team for surge/overflow support capacity, including onboarding their agents, maintaining documentation and macros they'll use, monitoring quality, and adjusting volume commitments as demand fluctuates.
Escalate effectively. Recognize which cases need to go beyond you—to Product or Engineering for a bug or root-cause fix, to Finance for a billing exception, or to leadership for a judgment call—and route them clearly rather than trying to resolve everything solo.
Partner with Product and Engineering. Surface recurring support themes, bugs, and friction points; represent the voice of the customer in roadmap conversations; validate fixes before they ship.
Track and report on support health. Own core support metrics (response time, resolution time, CSAT, ticket volume/drivers by category, cost per ticket) and report on them regularly to Operations leadership.
Scale the model. As volume grows across subscriptions, credits, and payments, help determine when and how to bring on additional internal headcount vs. lean further on outsourced operations, and help build out whatever tooling (help desk platform, macros, self-serve/FAQ content) is needed to keep up.

What We're Looking For

3-7 years of experience in payments operations, payments risk, fraud operations, billing operations, or customer operations for a high-volume consumer product, with hands-on experience resolving complex customer cases.
Experience with payments risk, fraud operations, disputes/chargebacks, or transaction monitoring in a consumer subscription, marketplace, gaming, virtual currency/credits, or digital-goods business.
Direct, hands-on experience actually working support tickets—not just managing a team that does.
Experience working with a payments/billing platform (Stripe or similar strongly preferred) and comfort navigating billing edge cases like disputes, refunds, and failed payments.
Experience managing or coordinating with a BPO or outsourced support vendor (TaskUs or similar) through standard operational KPIs is a strong plus.
Comfort operating cross-functionally with Product and Engineering: you can translate ticket and account patterns into clear, prioritized, data-informed feedback they'll actually act on.
A builder's mindset – you're energized by implementing a process where none exists yet, and comfortable doing so alongside others across the company who are already invested in getting it right.
Strong written communication – you'll be writing macros, documentation, and escalation summaries that other people (including vendor agents) rely on.
Comfortable with ambiguity and change – this function will look different in six months than it does today, and you'll be the one shaping that evolution.
Thrives in a fast-paced environment with minimal structure or oversight – you will set priorities with your manager, but do not need a manager checking in daily to stay on track.

Bonus

Strong data skills - ability to utilize dashboards to track metrics and do basic investigations to spot and explore problems; ability to build or edit SQL queries (or willingness/ability to learn)
Using AI to scale - experience optimizing workflows and processes by building or utilizing AI agents

new_jobs.title: Sales Operations Analyst
new_jobs.description:
A major enterprise organization, is seeking a Sales Operations Analyst to provide operational support to sales management. This role plans and coordinates projects that improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the sales organization, develops processes and procedures that support the sales process, and helps maintain the data and systems behind sales performance metrics.

This is a unified analyst role spanning Quote-to-Cash (Q2C) process support, SAP SD/MM administration, and Salesforce support. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, highly organized, and comfortable collaborating across Sales, Operations, and Finance in a fast-paced, enterprise-scale environment.

Responsibilities

Provide operational support to sales management and help plan/coordinate projects that improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the sales organization
Develop processes and procedures that support the sales process, and contribute to requirements for sales support systems
Maintain sales activity data that supports performance metrics and process improvement
Manage the evaluation pool and track related workflow
Coordinate with legal on drafting documents, with finance on approvals, and with sales reps to move items forward — tracking progress throughout
Process Return Merchandise Authorizations (RMAs)
Perform daily updating and tracking of orders, including internal orders processed through SAP
Support a recurring quarterly project focused on backlog and aging orders

Required Qualifications

Hands-on experience with the end-to-end Quote-to-Cash (Q2C) process — quote creation, order fulfillment, billing, and revenue recognition
Strong analytical skills — comfortable reviewing data, building pivot tables, and using VLOOKUP and similar functions
Strong written and oral communication skills, with the ability to work with both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team
Minimum of 2+ years of relevant professional experience; a university degree or equivalent practical experience

Preferred Qualifications

Functional experience with SAP SD (Sales & Distribution) and MM (Material Management) — standard transactions such as MM01, XD01, VA01, and VF01; SAP is trainable for a strong candidate without direct experience
Exposure to SAP S/4HANA, IDocs, BAPIs, or other integration mechanisms, including support for enhancements, data migration, or post-go-live stabilization
Salesforce administration experience, particularly Lightning UI and Sales Cloud — managing user permissions, custom fields/reports, and data hygiene; familiarity with Salesforce Data Loader; exposure to Salesforce CPQ is a plus
Experience supporting data migration, imports/exports, and data validation during system go-lives
Comfort working in fast-paced, cross-disciplinary teams with initiative and adaptability in ambiguous or changing environments
Awareness of compliance and data governance best practices related to master data and revenue recognition is a plus, though not required

Education

Some college preferred but not required
